overview: Pragmatic trial with individual allocation by a central office, in the 2027 intakes of a 24-week community strength and balance programme in 14 centres, comparing usual classes with classes plus an adherence support package.
population: Adults aged 65 and over starting the programme in 2027 who consent; people without a mobile phone and people with limited English are included, with phone calls and interpreters.
exposure: Adherence support package: weekly reminder by text or phone, a call within three days of any missed week, two calls from a trained peer volunteer (weeks 3 and 8), and a home exercise tick calendar reviewed by the instructor every four weeks.
procedures: After consent at the first class, the central office allocates each participant by computer-generated sequence stratified by centre, and informs the reminder coordinator; instructors see the calendar only for supported participants. Attendance comes from class registers; home exercise from the calendar (supported) and a two-question phone check at weeks 12 and 24 (both groups); falls from a monthly falls calendar returned by post or phone.

outcomes.name: Attendance
outcomes.measure: Attendance at 32 or more of 48 sessions, from class registers
outcomes.why: The behaviour the package targets and the condition for benefit.

outcomes.name: Home exercise days
outcomes.measure: Self-reported days of home exercise in the past week, two-question phone check
outcomes.why: The second target of the package (c2).

outcomes.name: Falls
outcomes.measure: Falls per person-year from monthly falls calendars
outcomes.why: What matters most to participants; reported descriptively (c3).

outcomes.name: Package delivery
outcomes.measure: Proportion of scheduled reminders, missed-week calls and peer calls delivered
outcomes.why: Separates a weak package from weak delivery.

outcomes.name: Exercise-related injury and pain flares
outcomes.measure: Participant-reported injuries or pain flares leading to a missed class
outcomes.why: More attendance should not bring more harm.

feasibility: About 43 people start each month; recruitment over about 14 months; reminders by the programme coordinator; peer calls by twelve trained volunteers; no extra work for instructors beyond reviewing calendars.
biasMitigation: Central allocation concealed from instructors until after consent
Primary outcome from existing registers kept by instructors for all participants
Phone checks by staff who do not deliver reminders

biasFlags.label: Contamination within classes
biasFlags.note: Shared classes; accepted and reported as part of the pragmatic question.

biasFlags.label: Instructor awareness
biasFlags.note: Instructors review calendars for supported participants; registers are kept as usual.

biasFlags.label: Thin prior evidence
biasFlags.note: Two retrieved studies; planning values are conservative.

flags: Centre and age group as the only adjustment variables
parsimony.simplestPath: Individual allocation, one register-based primary outcome, two secondary outcomes.

theoreticalFramework: Behaviour change techniques (prompts, self-monitoring, social support) named only to describe the package components with TIDieR.
summary: Pragmatic trial with register-based attendance as the primary outcome and falls reported descriptively.
